prose:
Latent Space's November 23–24 AINews roundup frames Gemini 4 Neon as a return to frontier competition, drawing on developer adoption anecdotes, vendor usage claims and third-party commentary. It also assembles research, model releases, harness comparisons, safety discussions and infrastructure updates from social accounts and community threads.

This is an aggregation, not independent reproduction of its many benchmarks or announcements. The roundup itself labels several rumors and disputed explanations, while some mathematical shorthand loses restrictions present in the original papers: the permanent claim, for example, requires attention to characteristic. Its reported harness dependence and cost variation are reasons not to read a single leaderboard as a universal ranking. Existing primary-source summaries remain the stronger record for the specific protein, mathematical and safety claims.
highlights: Neon framing is an editorial assessment
Adoption figures remain attributed to their reporting sources
Issue samples social accounts and selected communities
Unreleased-model sightings and crypto rumors are unconfirmed
Harness and time-budget choices can change rankings
Mathematical shorthand does not replace theorem scope
Siren percentages refer to different evaluation settings
No model or infrastructure release was installed or tested
